Here are the key facts I was able to find about Mats Nilsson, the Swedish javelin thrower:

- Mats Nilsson was a Swedish javelin thrower who competed in the 1980s and early 1990s.

- He won the gold medal in the javelin throw at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul, South Korea with a throw of 86.34 meters.

- This Olympic gold medal was the highlight of Nilsson's career. He was considered one of the top javelin throwers in the world during this time period.

- Nilsson also won silver medals in the javelin throw at the 1987 World Championships in Athletics and the 1990 European Championships in Athletics.

- He held the world record in the javelin throw briefly in 1987 with a throw of 89.10 meters, though this record was soon broken by other athletes.

- Nilsson represented Sweden at three Summer Olympic Games - 1984, 1988, and 1992. His gold medal in 1988 was his greatest achievement.

- Beyond these key competitive results, I don't have much additional detailed information about Mats Nilsson's personal life or the specifics of his training and development as an athlete. My knowledge is limited to his main accomplishments as a top international javelin thrower in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
